parts.part: whole settlement (square stone settlement wall with bastions and the central residential complex)
parts.layout_phase: the single Harappan (Sorath-type, Late Mature) occupation; the excavators' report, in press, has not been seen, and no sub-phases are published
parts.what_was_built: Kotada Bhadli, in Nakhatrana taluka of Kachchh, is a 3.11 ha settlement inside a stone wall, excavated in 2010-2013 by the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute with the Gujarat State Department of Archaeology. The first season found 'a cultural sequence of 60cm, surrounded by a nearly intact square fortification wall' and exposed a four-walled room and the inner face of the southern wall (IAR 2010-11, pp. 30-31). In 2012-13 the outer face of the southern wall, a middle bastion, a south-western corner bastion and a probable gate at the south-eastern corner were exposed, together with the inner wall and a rectangular residential complex of nine rooms (IAR 2012-13, pp. 27-28). Chakraborty, a member of the excavation team, describes 'a huge stone-built wall surrounding the settlement', about 3 to 3.5 m wide without its central pillar, with stone and rubble houses at the centre and no mud bricks (Chakraborty 2019, pp. 46-47). Along the inner face of the southern wall the layers are: layer 9, 'a layer mixed with ash on which the wall was built'; layers 6 and 8, compact and sterile, 'probably created as a foundation for the wall'; and occupation layers 7, 5, 4, 3 and 2 that accumulated against the wall and belong to the same cultural period as the single occupation layer (layer 3) of the residential area (p. 63).
parts.locator: iar2010-11 pp. 30-31; iar2012-13 pp. 27-28; chakraborty2019kachchh pp. 46-49, 63-65
parts.excavator_basis: Radiocarbon. Chakraborty dates the walled settlement from three AMS dates on charcoal from layers that formed after the wall was built: 'the walled site might have been occupied between 2300-1950 BCE, or 4350-3900 BP' (Chakraborty 2019, p. 65). He also places the site in the Late Mature or Urban-to-Post-Urban transition on its Sorath-type pottery and comparisons with Kanmer IIB and III, Shikarpur II and Dholavira Stage VI (p. 65). The excavators' own report (Shirvalkar and Rawat, in press) was not available to us.

radiocarbon.context: sample KTB/AMS-5, trench -XO3, depth 4.2 m below datum, layer 9; 'acquired from outside of the settlement wall in layer 9' (text calls the sample KTB/CH-5)
radiocarbon.phase: layer 9, the ashy layer on which the settlement wall was built; 'most likely formed before the wall was built and may indicate the earliest occupation'
radiocarbon.note: F14C printed as 0.6186±0.0033. The thesis does not name the half-life; the printed ages equal -8033 x ln(F14C), the conventional age on the 5568-year half-life. Measured at the AMS facility of the University of Ottawa.

radiocarbon.context: sample KTB/AMS-2, trench -XM3, depth 3.61 m below datum, layer 3; near the southern settlement wall
radiocarbon.phase: occupation layer formed after the wall was built
radiocarbon.note: F14C printed as 0.6285±0.0034; half-life inferred as for UOC-4158.

radiocarbon.context: sample KTB/AMS-3, trench -XJ11, depth 4.05 m below datum, layer 5; near the southern settlement wall
radiocarbon.phase: occupation layer formed after the wall was built
radiocarbon.note: F14C printed as 0.6327±0.0034; half-life inferred as for UOC-4158.

radiocarbon.context: sample KTB/AMS-4, trench -XB2, depth 4.2 m below datum, layer 3A; the sample from the residential area
radiocarbon.phase: occupation layer of the residential area, after the wall was built
radiocarbon.note: F14C printed as 0.6264±0.0034; half-life inferred as for UOC-4158. The text says one of the four dated samples came from the residential area and three from near the southern wall (p. 64); the table does not mark which, and we infer from the layer number (3A) that it is this one.

parts.conflicts: Chakraborty reports that 'Unpublished dates from this settlement suggest that it was occupied between 4200-3900 YBP (Pokharia 2017)' (p. 46), slightly later than his own 4350-3900 BP for the walled settlement (p. 65), and says his three post-wall dates match those unpublished dates. The sample from layer 9 is called KTB/CH-5 in the text and KTB/AMS-5 in the table (pp. 64, 67).

first_occupation.phase: the single Harappan occupation; the pre-wall ash of layer 9 may mark slightly earlier activity
first_occupation.basis: Radiocarbon: 'the overall 2σ range of dates from the site falls between 2450-1950 BCE' (Chakraborty 2019, p. 64), including the layer 9 date UOC-4158 (2464-2206 cal BCE) from below the wall. Chakraborty adds that there is 'no indication in terms of structural or material remains to support an earlier occupation at the settlement prior to the building of the settlement wall, apart from a few layers of ashy sediments mixed with tiny charcoal pieces' (p. 64).

sources.citation: Chakraborty, K. S. 2019. Subsistence-Based Economy and the Regional Interaction Processes of the Indus Civilization Borderland in Kachchh, Gujarat: A Bio-Molecular Perspective. PhD thesis, Department of Anthropology, University of Toronto. Section 2.3 and Table 2.1, pp. 63-67. Pages cited are the thesis's printed page numbers.

Archaeological Survey of India. Indian Archaeology 2010-11 - A Review. New Delhi: Archaeological Survey of India. Gujarat, entry 9, 'Excavation at Kotada Bhadli, District Kachchh', printed pp. 30-31 onward (PDF pp. 41-43).
Archaeological Survey of India. Indian Archaeology 2012-13 - A Review. New Delhi: Archaeological Survey of India. Gujarat, entry 9, 'Excavations at Kotada Bhadli, District Kachchh', pp. 27-28.

notes: Kotada Bhadli was occupied once, for a short time, and the settlement wall and the houses inside it belong to that single occupation; there is no earlier town under it. Its layout phase is therefore the whole Harappan occupation, which its pottery places among the Sorath-type settlements of the Late Mature phase. The dates come from a PhD thesis by a member of the excavation team, not from the excavators' report, which is cited as in press (Shirvalkar and Rawat, eds, Excavation at Kotada Bhadli, Taluka Nakhatrana, District Kachchh, Gujarat (2010-2014), Archaeological Survey of India). We did not find it published. The layer 9 date (UOC-4158) is the best estimate for activity just before the wall was built. The three dates from deposits laid against the wall or after it was built (UOC-4155, -4156, -4157) date its use. Together they place construction after the layer 9 date (2464-2206 cal BCE) and before or near the earliest post-wall range (2295-2033 cal BCE); this bracket is our reading of the published ranges, not a published model. The Pokharia et al. 2017 dates mentioned by Chakraborty were not traced. Chakraborty also comments on the orientation of the houses; per our brief we did not record it.
